summary: This informational RFC defines a pair of reciprocal link relation types, item and collection, expressing the relationship between a collection and its members on the Web, building on RFC 5988.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines two link labels for collections and their members. An item link points to a member, and a collection link points back to a collection.

questions: what are item and collection link relations
how do link relations describe collections
can something be both an item and a collection
subtitle: Defines reciprocal Web link relations for a collection and its members.

tldr.problem: Web resources needed shared link relation names for connecting a collection to its members and members back to collections.
tldr.mechanism: The item relation points from a collection to a member; collection points from a member to a collection.
tldr.outcome: The two names are registered for use across media types under the Web Linking framework.

today: RFC 6573 is an Informational RFC. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Links Between Collections and Members
sections.content:
RFC 5988 standardized a way to indicate relationships between Web resources. RFC 6573 defines two reciprocal link relation types to express the relationship between a collection and its members.

The relations can be used across different media types. The RFC names OpenSearch, Maze+XML and Collection+JSON as examples of formats that use them.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC names two relationships between Web resources. They can describe a collection, a member, or both.

sections.title: The item Relation
sections.content:
When a resource represents a collection, an item link relation identifies a target resource that represents one member of that collection. For example, a product catalog may link to resources for individual products.

The link may appear in a representation or an HTTP Link header. A collection can include one or more item links.
sections.plainLanguage: An item link starts from a collection and points to one of its members. A catalog could use it to link to product resources.

sections.title: The collection Relation
sections.content:
When a resource represents a member, a collection link relation identifies a target collection of which the context resource is a member. A resource may belong to multiple collections, so it may have multiple collection links.

The target need not be a list; it can be a document with details about the collection. A link can represent both an item in one collection and a collection itself, so both relation values may apply.
sections.plainLanguage: A collection link starts from a member and points to a collection. A resource can use both relation names if it is itself a collection and belongs to another one.
